title: Tenant throttling playbook and reservation rebalance after capacity surge
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: During a production capacity surge on 2026-02-24 a single tenant running a bursty batch workload saturated a dedicated cluster reservation, triggering broad tail latency increases and a partial eviction cascade. Root causes: (1) reservation sizing was based on stale 50th-percentile usage; (2) soft-burst policy allowed temporary allocation spikes up to 3x without proper backpressure; (3) no tenant-level leaky-bucket throttling or per-tenant p99 saturation alerting. This ticket consolidates the post-incident action items into an operational playbook and engineering work to prevent recurrence. Action items (owners and targets): 1) Implement tenant-level backpressure/leaky-bucket throttler (owner: Noah Patel, ETA: 2026-03-12) — enforce sustained QPS limits and smooth bursts. 2) Reservation rebalance job (owner: Priya Singh, ETA: 2026-03-20) — daily historical analysis using 95th/99th percentiles to propose reservation adjustments and nudges to customers. 3) Harden burst policy defaults (owner: Ethan Park, ETA: 2026-03-10) — change default soft-burst cap to 1.5x and require explicit opt-in for >1.5x with documented SLAs. 4) Monitoring & alerts (owner: Lina Rodríguez, ETA: 2026-03-05) — add Datadog monitors for reservation utilization >90% for 5m, sustained bursting >10s, and tenant-level KV cache pressure. 5) Autoscaler backoff and eviction containment (owner: Alex Becker, ETA: 2026-03-18) — add staged backoff and tenant cgroup weight limits to avoid eviction cascades. 6) Playbook & runbook updates (owner: Maya Chen, ETA: 2026-03-08) — include triage steps, escalation matrix, and rollback guidance. Each action item includes a follow-up PR, staging validation, and a canary rollout plan. Links to artifacts, dashboards, and PRs are in attachments. The goal is to reduce single-tenant blast radius, make reservation sizing adaptive, and ensure predictable degradation instead of widespread latency spikes.
comments: 2026-02-25: Initial incident review completed. Timeline reconstructed from Datadog traces and runtime logs. Noted reservation hit 100% at 2026-02-24T14:11Z; evictions began at 14:13Z.

2026-02-26: Postmortem meeting — consensus that upstream customer workload caused sustained high-seq bursts. Agreed on a two-track approach: immediate throttling + longer-term reservation rebalance automation.

2026-03-01: Prototype leaky-bucket implemented in staging. Early tests show 30-40% reduction in p99 latency for neighboring tenants under synthetic burst load. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4521
2026-03-05: Monitoring alerts added to staging and prod (Datadog dashboards): https://app.datadog.com/dash/cluster/capacity-surge. Lina validated signal fidelity against replayed traces.
2026-03-08: Playbook draft uploaded to Confluence for review: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFR/Reserved+Capacity+Surge+Playbook. PM review requested (Priya).
2026-03-10: Burst policy change PR opened to reduce default soft-burst cap and require opt-in: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/1193. Eng lead review pending.
2026-03-11: Staging canary run for reservation rebalance job completed; proposal generation is stable. Edge-case: short-lived spike patterns create noisy suggestions — will add smoothing window.
2026-03-12: Decision: ship throttler and monitoring alerts to prod as hotfix, then follow with rebalance job and burst policy changes. Rollout plan in comments below.
resolution: Immediate mitigations (throttler + alerts) scheduled for prod rollout week of 2026-03-13. Reservation rebalance automation and burst policy hardening to follow; owners assigned. After production rollout we'll measure 30-day 95th/99th latency and reservation saturation metrics to validate reductions in tenant blast radius. Close ticket when: (1) throttler and alerts are in prod and passing canary, (2) rebalance proposals are auto-generated and triaged for the top 20 clusters, (3) burst policy defaults updated and documented.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (hotfix): deploy tenant throttler to 10% of clusters (canary) -> monitor p99/p50 and eviction rates for 48h -> expand to 100% if stable.
Phase 2: enable reservation rebalance proposals in read-only mode for ops review for 7 days -> collect feedback -> enable automated suggestions with manual approval.
Phase 3: rollout burst policy default changes with customer opt-in and migration notes; notify impacted customers 2 weeks in advance.
